mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate sales (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following a sustained decline in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following an INDPRO increase > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a single month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances following a PAYEMS increase > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) shows an annual increase of less than 2%, it signals a potential disinflationary environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real interest rates become more favorable.
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in > 50% of instances meeting the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) shows a quarter-over-quarter decline and retail sales (RSAFS) also decline over the same period, it signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decline quarter-over-quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances meeting the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in a single month and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 150,000 in the same month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3% and PAYEMS increases > 150,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances meeting the trigger conditions.
